citations.quote: Jakafi is a kinase inhibitor indicated for treatment of patients with intermediate or high-risk myelofibrosis, including primary myelofibrosis, post-polycythemia vera myelofibrosis and post-essential thrombocythemia myelofibrosis. (1)

target_moa.text: Ruxolitinib is a kinase inhibitor that inhibits Janus Associated Kinases JAK1 and JAK2, which mediate signaling of cytokines and growth factors important for hematopoiesis and immune function; myelofibrosis is associated with dysregulated JAK1 and JAK2 signaling.

citations.quote: Ruxolitinib, a kinase inhibitor, inhibits Janus Associated Kinases (JAKs) JAK1 and JAK2 which mediate the signaling of a number of cytokines and growth factors that are important for hematopoiesis and immune function.
Myelofibrosis (MF) is a myeloproliferative neoplasm (MPN) known to be associated with dysregulated JAK1 and JAK2 signaling.

Jakafi™ (ruxolitinib) is a new molecular entity and the first of a new class of kinase inhibitors, that of JAK1 and JAK2 kinases, which act in signaling pathways involved in myeloid cell proliferation.

citations.quote: An Oncology Drugs Advisory Committee meeting is not planned for this submission, because the benefits of ruxolitinib in spleen volume reduction and symptom control are evident in the results of two adequate and well-controlled trials, while adverse reactions appear to be manageable.

description.text: Labeling update adding 3-year median follow-up overall survival data and dose titration/modification information (no new indication)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for updates to the package insert that include overall survival data based on 3 year median follow-up from the two randomized Phase 3 studies, INCB 18424-351 and INCB 18424-352 (CINC424A2352), and dose titration information based on experience in these 2 studies. In addition, the Dosage and Administration section has been updated to include dose modifications for patients who are on a stable dose of Jakafi® and then start treatment with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor or fluconazole. Lastly, additional text has been added to the Warnings and Precautions Sections 5.2 and 5.3.
